reduction: n: IAPWS R9-97's eq. 1 at 298.15 K and 997.0476 kg m⁻³, evaluated at each wavelength of 380–780 nm every 5 nm, to six significant figures (decision-r08-t5g ruling 1); λ is read as the vacuum wavelength (read as the air wavelength, n would fall by at most 1.2 × 10⁻⁵, at 380 nm, and by under 5 × 10⁻⁶ from 595 nm, inside the release's uncertainty). The release's estimated uncertainty (its Table 2, the liquid at ambient pressure): 1.5 × 10⁻⁵ over 0.40–0.70 µm at 5–60 °C, 5 × 10⁻⁴ over 0.21–0.40 µm and 10⁻³ over 0.70–1.1 µm. Checks: Daimon and Masumura 2007's formula for distilled water at 24.0 °C (Appl. Opt. 46, 3811, DOI 10.1364/AO.46.003811; refractiveindex.info, main/H2O/nk/Daimon-24.0C.yml, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/polyanskiy/refractiveindex.info-database/c5c2f188e848453def5970e347399d653df2ffc2/database/data/main/H2O/nk/Daimon-24.0C.yml, SHA-256 1d41f6f3b8a6702e6b3b788b4d2138f9ae7730305802cea2d93e91f38c7ff7c7, fetched 2026-10-15) lies −5.6 × 10⁻⁶ at 380 nm, +1.1 × 10⁻⁷ at 550 nm, +2.6 × 10⁻⁶ at 780 nm from R9-97 at 24 °C and 997.2994 kg m⁻³ (the same isobar); Quan and Fry 1995's pure water (S = 0, 25 °C, relative to air), times dry air's index at 15 °C (Peck and Reeder 1972's standard air), lies above it by 1.7 × 10⁻⁵ to 3.5 × 10⁻⁵ over 400–700 nm, and by 6.8 × 10⁻⁵ at 380 nm and 8.9 × 10⁻⁵ at 780 nm, beyond their range. R08.T5.h's change from Hale and Querry's n (G. M. Hale and M. R. Querry, "Optical constants of water in the 200-nm to 200-µm wavelength region", Appl. Opt. 12 (1973) 555–563, DOI 10.1364/AO.12.000555), which R08.T5.g's file held: +0.00451 at 380 nm, +0.00119 at 550 nm and −0.00132 at 780 nm, so n(380) − n(780) is 0.01663 where it was 0.0108. k = aλ ÷ 4π, to six significant figures (decision-r08-t5g ruling 2): Mason, Cone and Fry 2016's Table 2 over 380–495 nm, linear in log a between its rows every 2 nm (a three-point moving average of rows every 2 nm, at 23 ± 0.5 °C: Mason's dissertation pp. 75 and 80); Pope and Fry 1997's rows over 500–725 nm, every grid point on a row (at 22 °C); and Kou et al. 1993's over 730–780 nm, every 5 nm (at 22 °C), as IOCCG 2018 lists them (A. R. Neeley and A. Mannino (eds.), "Inherent Optical Property Measurements and Protocols: Absorption Coefficient", IOCCG Protocol Series vol. 1.0 (IOCCG, Dartmouth, 2018), DOI 10.25607/OBP-119, Table 1.1). The seam at 495/500 nm is where the two cross: Pope and Fry's 0.0173 m⁻¹ at 495 nm lies between Mason et al.'s 0.01648 and 0.01774 at 494 and 496 nm, and their 0.0204 at 500 nm within 1.6% of Mason et al.'s 0.02073. The seam at 725/730 nm is IOCCG's: Kou et al. run about 0.04 m⁻¹ above Pope and Fry at 670 nm and 0.07 m⁻¹ at 725 nm over their overlap (IOCCG §1.1.1), and IOCCG keeps Pope and Fry there, as this file does. R08.T5.h's change from R08.T5.g's file, whose k was Pope and Fry's over 380–725 nm and Hale and Querry's from 750 nm, log-linear between over 730–745 nm: k falls by a factor of 7.95 at 380 nm, 2.99 at 400 nm, 1.22 at 440 nm, and rises by 1.30 at 740 nm, 1.09 at 750 nm, 1.17 at 780 nm; Hale and Querry give nothing to this file. The alternative below 500 nm is Pope and Fry's, which runs 7.95 at 380 nm, 2.99 at 400 nm, 1.46 at 420 nm, 1.22 at 440 nm, 1.08 at 460 nm, 1.05 at 480 nm, 0.98 at 500 nm, 1.04 at 520 nm, 1.00 at 540 nm, 1.00 at 550 nm times Mason et al.'s: the original integrating cavity's sensitivity falls slowly over 410–500 nm and rapidly below 410 nm, and Mason et al. agree with Pope and Fry above 440 nm (Mason's dissertation pp. 81–89); the IOCCG protocol (§1.1.1–1.1.2) takes Pope and Fry as the state of the art over about 420–725 nm only, their ultraviolet values "significantly higher than these other careful works, indicating possible contamination". Mason et al.'s 520, 540 and 550 nm rows are the cross-check of Pope and Fry's there. Temperatures: k is at 23 °C to 495 nm and 22 °C from 500 nm, n at 25 °C. Below 550 nm water's temperature coefficient is near zero; near 740 nm it is 0.0161 m⁻¹ °C⁻¹ (IOCCG's Table 1.1, after Röttgers et al. 2014), so 22 → 25 °C would raise a there by about 1.7%, not drawn (one temperature per liquid)
